title: Warren Buffett at Florida: moats, circle of competence, and picking who to be
summary: Buffett tells UF MBA students that character and habits matter more than IQ, then explains how he picks businesses: simple, understandable, with a widening moat and honest management. He covers Long-Term Capital's collapse, avoiding macro forecasts, concentration, and his mistakes of omission.

principles.text: Character and habits are chosen; copy admired traits early, before the chains of habit get too heavy.
principles.quote: the chains of habit are too light to be felt until they're too heavy to be broken.

principles.text: Never risk what you have and need to gain what you don't need.
principles.quote: to make the money they didn't have and didn't need, they risked what they did have and did need. And that's foolish.

principles.text: Look for a castle with a durable moat run by an honest, able manager; widen the moat over time.
principles.quote: I want a business with a moat around it. I want a very valuable castle in the middle. And then I want the duke who's in charge of that castle to be honest and hard working and able.

principles.text: Stay inside your circle of competence; its size matters less than knowing its edges.
principles.quote: The important thing is not how big the circle is. The important thing is staying inside the circle.

principles.text: Focus on what is important and knowable; ignore macro and interest rate predictions.
principles.quote: what you really want to do in investments is figure out what's important and knowable. If it's unimportant or unknowable, you you forget about it.

principles.text: Buy a business you'd hold if the market closed for years; stocks are part ownership, not tickers.
principles.quote: I don't want to buy any stock where if they close the New York Stock Exchange tomorrow for 5 years, I won't be happy owning it.
